rationale: Pre-registered acceptance limits for the ws1-voice realtime models against their offline truth models. Committed before the realtime models are evaluated. They are numerical solver tolerances, not analog tolerances: the truth models implement the same declared (partly inferred) circuit equations, so agreement validates the solver, not the circuit. Each stage lists its grid so the limits cannot be re-scoped after evaluation.

ig00156_nodal.description: Plan step 1.1b. Realtime src/core/Ig00156Filter.h versus the offline nodal truth model src/reference/IG00156Network.h (4 states per stage: input coupling, 180 pF branch, two integrators).
ig00156_nodal.equivalence_note: Time-domain realtime output (float) versus the truth model's exact trapezoidal step with the same prewarp, small-signal multi-sine, normalized by the output peak.
ig00156_nodal.small_signal_core_band: 0.5..2 x cutoff and at most fs/8; complex error normalized by the truth response peak
ig00156_nodal.small_signal_band: 20 Hz .. min(20 kHz, fs/5); hi_rate applies at internal rates >= 192 kHz
ig00156_nodal.nonlinear_fixture: 96 kHz internal, cutoff 1 kHz, Q 5 and Q 1; sines of 0.5/1 kHz at 1.0 and 2.5 engine units; truth = implicit trapezoid with full Newton at 16x oversampling; RMS of difference over the last 0.1 s of 1.5 s, divided by truth RMS
ig00156_nodal.q_anchor_fixture: Pole-derived Q of the nodal truth stage at a 200 Hz total cutoff: Q(VQ = 0 V) = 5 and Q(VQ = 10 V) = 0.5 (CS-80 service p42), both stages
ig00156_nodal.cutoff_anchor_fixture: Pole natural frequency of the truth stage at the documented control points 0.25 V/5 V, 0.5 V/5 V, 0.25 V/6 V (gm part 1 kHz, 2 kHz, 2 kHz) plus the 22.575 Hz feedforward contribution, Q = 5

Square (50 %) WSC pulse 3 Vpp, C1 at 2' (261.6 Hz), alignment of SourceFactoryTones.h, physical (un-normalized) stage gains, declared mix-node fixture: open-circuit (saw + pulse) / 2 behind 75 kOhm. A miss is reported, never fitted.

oscillator_segment_cache.description: 2026-11-01 pre-registration. Event-root caching may reuse the next root only inside an analytic oscillator segment. Check a long settled static run and parameter-change/idle-wake edge cases against the existing independent waveform, event-time and alias gates; all numerical outputs remain subject to the old tolerances.
oscillator_segment_cache.stable_fixture: 96 kHz internal, 261.6 Hz settled waveform, saw and pulse enabled, neutral threshold, 4096 consecutive ticks. The unoptimized per-tick root solver is called at least 4096 times; a segment cache must solve only at actual branch/reset boundaries, with headroom for knot, fold and pulse events.
oscillator_segment_cache.invalidation_fixture: A cutoff/pulse-threshold/gate edit, idle-advance and exact state restore must invalidate cached branch roots before they can be reused. Existing exact control-change and idle-wake fixtures continue to bind audible numerical behavior.

engine_dc_coefficient_cache.description: 2026-11-01 pre-registration before hoisting the legacy 10 Hz DC-blocker coefficient from the internal sample loop to rate preparation. This is a software performance optimization with no revised analog law or source-engine sound allowance.
engine_dc_coefficient_cache.coefficient_fixture: At host rates 44.1/48/96 kHz, all Legacy/Source Performance oversampling choices, and render-time quality/offline mode changes, the cached float must equal the original per-tick expression std::exp(-kTwoPi * 10.0f * (1.0f / static_cast<float>(internalRate))) exactly. No substituted double arithmetic, equivalent pole approximations or changed rounding are permitted.
engine_dc_coefficient_cache.audio_fixture: The existing scripts/check-compat-gates.sh --strict-v2 governs literal byte identity of Legacy default, Legacy tails, V1 circuit numerics and pinned V2 audio. The hoist must change none of these bytes; any intentional later VCA/oscillator re-pin is independently accounted for.

ig00151_vca.description: Plan step 1.4. Circuit-engine IG00151 voice VCA (src/core/Vca.h): linear LI input with its 10 nF node, exponential EI input, declared offset and CV feedthrough, constant-power rank pan.
ig00151_vca.linear_fixture: static gain proportional to the settled LI control at fixed EI and envelope; ratio error at 0.25/0.5/1/2 x
ig00151_vca.exponential_fixture: gain ratio 2^(delta EI) at fixed LI, EI steps -1..+1 octave
ig00151_vca.li_tau_fixture: LI step response reaches 1 - 1/e at the declared ideal-source Thevenin RC of the five documented level branches and the 10 nF pin capacitor, at 88.2/96/192 kHz
ig00151_vca.pedestal_fixture: zero-signal output (offset plus CV feedthrough) at full LI 2.6 and envelope 1, relative to a unit signal at the same gain
ig00151_vca.closed_discharge_fixture: 2026-11-01 pre-registration: a VCA whose envelope has just reached zero still drives the downstream 1 uF/100 k coupling capacitor. The closed-output recurrence must match process(input=0, envelope=0) sample by sample across 88.2/96/192 kHz, after a 200 ms charged pedestal and a fast released envelope. This is a declared circuit-model inference, not hardware evidence.
ig00151_vca.closed_handoff_fixture: The first idle sample following the last envelope-zero sample must continue the capacitor's exponential discharge. The difference from the physical one-sample recurrence, and the boundary step for a charged pedestal, must be at most 1e-6 engine units; a hard mute of the coupling output is explicitly forbidden.
ig00151_vca.closed_engine_tail_fixture: 2026-11-01 pre-registration, 48 kHz source policy: compare identically clocked engine twins with silent oscillators but the declared VCA pedestal. At the first frame with no active voices, apply a deliberate All Sound Off hard panic to one twin only; compare the next 50 ms of output. Without hidden source differences, the unpanicked voice must pass the AC-coupling discharge through the engine mix, yielding a peak inter-stream difference above the 1e-9 normalized-output numerical detection floor. The deliberately panicked twin must remain mute. This lower bound detects disconnected idle-output wiring, not calibrated analogue audibility.
ig00151_vca.pan_fixture: L^2 + R^2 constant over pan -1..1; exactly 0.5 per side at centre
ig00151_vca.click_fixture: cs80_engine_audit --suite phrase, policy source, every row at 44.1/48/96 kHz, columns click_steal and click_retrigger

tolerance_drift.description: Plan step 2.5 (registered 2026-10-31 by the integrator before implementation). Circuit-engine per-card component tolerances and thermal drift (src/core/ToleranceModel.h). Declared distributions, not measured units: resistors 5 %, capacitors 10 %, truncated normal with sigma = tol / 2 and truncation at +/- tol.
tolerance_drift.draw_fixture: 4096 cards from consecutive seeds: sample standard deviation of every resistor and capacitor draw within 10 % of its declared sigma (2.5 % R, 5 % C); sample mean within 3 standard errors of zero
tolerance_drift.draw_erratum: Corrected before evaluation, limit unchanged: a normal truncated at +/- 2 sigma has a standard deviation of 0.8796 sigma, so the sample standard deviation is compared with 0.8796 x the declared sigma (the first text compared it with sigma itself, which the declared truncation can never meet).
tolerance_drift.mapping_fixture: cutoff ratio = 1 / sqrt(c1 c2) per stage, Q ratio = sqrt(c1 / c2), level ratio = (1 + rf) / (1 + rin), envelope time ratio = (1 + r)(1 + c), each raised to the dispersion scale VOICE DISPERSION / 0.35
tolerance_drift.engine_fixture: rendered RankInfo cutoffs and Q of a held note at dispersion 0.35 equal the nominal values times the card's ratios (source policy); PURE CS-80 and dispersion 0 give ratios of exactly 1
tolerance_drift.determinism: identical card draws for every host rate, oversampling factor, prepare and reset
tolerance_drift.drift_psd_fixture: log-log least-squares slope of the drift process's periodogram (Welch, Hann, 8 segments x 32 cards of 2^16 control samples at 100 Hz) between 0.003 and 0.3 Hz
tolerance_drift.drift_psd_erratum: Corrected before evaluation, limits unchanged: the first text named 2^14 control samples split into 8 segments (20 s each, 0.05 Hz resolution), which cannot resolve the registered 0.003 Hz band edge; each segment is now 2^16 samples (655 s).
tolerance_drift.drift_rms_fixture: RMS of the warm thermal drift (warm-up excluded) at ANALOG DRIFT 0.25 over 32 cards x 600 s; declared target 2 cents
tolerance_drift.warmup_fixture: the warm-up offset falls to 1/e of its start at the declared 120 s time constant
tolerance_drift.worn_unit_fixture: the worn-unit drift model reproduces the historical 0.031 Hz sine law (drift x 0.9 semitones, phase offsets 0.73 per voice) sample for sample
tolerance_drift.worn_unit_erratum: Clarified before evaluation, limit unchanged: 'sample for sample' is checked against the Legacy policy's rendered oscillator frequency at the same settings (the historical law in the same float pipeline), because an analytic recomputation outside the engine cannot match float readouts to 1e-4 cents.
